<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **61** documentable anchor(s).

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 43 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a018ddcc6c3c5d6c62342a53fc0bdb8002ae7971` — the merge of head `bd194d3ffcc734a0c0feb32dc86166ba97a12cd5` into base `411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a018ddcc6c3c5d6c62342a53fc0bdb8002ae7971 && git checkout a018ddcc6c3c5d6c62342a53fc0bdb8002ae7971
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719 bd194d3ffcc734a0c0feb32dc86166ba97a12cd5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719 && git merge --no-ff bd194d3ffcc734a0c0feb32dc86166ba97a12cd5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 411646562566a1e12b4e0fc3de256192e8302719` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `14bf9f91364c962a6dc96e3e66272c95ed29e14d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts

Security-touching: this is the record-sharing write gate and the predicate write's floor decision (authorization). It was judged on one question first: can the set form answer `allow` where the per-row gate would not. By reading, it cannot.

Check-runs on this head when read: 20 success, 11 skipped, 34 in progress, 0 failed. The PR is a draft. Every Test Core shard, Build Core and the workspace type check were still running, so this PASS is the design verdict only; it weighs no red gate because none had concluded. Do not queue before those runs end green.

### ① Derived judgments

- Public surface: `ISharingService` gains two optional members, `checkEditMany` and `checkDeleteMany`, each `(object, recordIds, context)` answering `SharingWriteVerdict[]`. Right. No existing member, type or export changes shape. No write-scope member (`buildWriteFilter`) is added, as ruling 7190344023 (option C) requires.
- Accept set: unchanged. No authorable key or schema moves, and `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
- Rows written: unchanged by design. Plugin-security drops the floor for exactly the ids whose verdict is `allow`, as before; the sharing middleware's own write scope is untouched.
- Behaviour that does move, all in the closed direction:
  - A fault now denies a whole chunk (up to 1,000 ids), or the whole list at the plugin-security seam, where the per-row path denied one row. This is the ruled term.
  - By id, an update on an object with a queue column reads the row once, not twice. No by-id path gains a read.
- `docs/adr/**` and `skills/**` are not in the diff. ADR-0155 is untouched, and no leaf is put in any find.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). Right: an additive optional member on a published contract. The line is in both the PR body and the changeset.

`patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` and `@objectstack/plugin-security` is right under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. All three packages are moved by the diff. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.

One observation for the lane seat, not graded here: the changeset's "from 20,004 store reads and 6.6 s" is the per-row run on this branch (6,603 ms). The same case on main read 6,013 ms, and the #35802 changeset says 5.3 s. The read counts agree everywhere.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7193076972 carries no `open_questions` and `security_findings: none`. Its four deviations (no empty-branch probe, `check:dev-prereqs` not measured, ablation 4 run before the merge, bench uncommitted) do not touch the contract. Accepted.
- Member names, under the maintainer's veto window: `checkEditMany` / `checkDeleteMany` follow the ruled precedent (`checkEdit` / `checkDelete` plus the data protocol's optional `…Many`). Two members, not one with a verb argument, matches how this contract already splits the verdict. No objection; the veto stays the maintainer's.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The set form materialises no new ids: it is handed the candidate list plugin-security already holds and already binds into the write. Per chunk it makes one `id IN (…)` read and, for update, one `record_id IN (…)` read. The alternative push-down, the share semi-join leaf in a find, is what ADR-0155 Q3 forbids and ruling C rules out. The owner match is done in the app against an owner set resolved once, because the tri-state needs per-id facts (missing row, null owner, queue) that a filtered read would hide. Reason given.
- Ruled premise (at most two store reads per chunk plus one bypass probe per call, chunk of at least 1,000): holds by reading. Outside the chunk loop the call adds one owner-set resolution and one membership lookup per distinct (queue, organization); neither grows per row. The 24-read figure follows (10 chunks × 2, plus the write's own 4). The timings were not re-measured.
- `WRITE_VERDICT_CHUNK` docblock: the Oracle and SQL Server bounds it cites were not verified in the driver. The chunk is within both as stated, so nothing depends on it.
- Out-of-scope question 1, the docs gap: real. `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx` lists `buildReadFilter`, `canEdit`, `canDelete` and `canManageShares` only. It has never listed `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` (a gap since #6428), and this PR adds two more unlisted members. It is outside the card's file surface. File a docs follow-up that adds the tri-state members and the set form together.
- Out-of-scope question 2, `.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`: its cost paragraph ("one sharing verdict, a few store reads, for each matched row", and the 1,000 / 10,000-row figures) is now stale for the bundled sharing service, and both changesets ship in the same release. It stays true only for a sharing service without the set form. Not wrong enough to block: this PR's changeset states the new cost and names the old figures as "went from". Recommended: a dedicated correction of that paragraph before the release consumes it, saying the per-row cost applies where the service serves no set form. That edit needs the seat's deliberate-correction declaration, so it is the seat's call, not a rider here.
- 2a (card #37535) is not in this diff. Right.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts`** against ruling 7190344023. Holds, term by term:
- Set form of the write verdict, per id the same tri-state: `answer[i]` is the verdict for `recordIds[i]`, same length, same order.
- No write-scope member.
- Optional, feature-detected, per-row fallback with the same answers.
- The service owns the chunking.
- A chunk whose lookup throws is `deny`, never `abstain`.
- The delete form carries the verb boundary (ADR-0111 D3).

Both docblocks name the `modifyAllRecords` bypass, which the spec parity test now requires of them.

**`plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts`** against the contract. I tried to break the equality between `writeVerdicts` over a list and the per-row gate on main, class by class:
- One implementation: `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` are `writeVerdicts` over one id. I compared that one-id path with main's bodies line by line. The decision order is the same: system `allow`, bypass-listed `abstain`, no schema `abstain`, queue (update only) before the open-OWD `abstain`, no owner field `abstain`, no principal `deny`, owner at write depth, write-level share (update only, and only where grants count), Modify All last.
- Owner and role hierarchy: the same `matchesOwnerScope`, with the owner set resolved once per call. `org` depth still needs a row with an owner.
- Sharing rules, manual shares, teams: the gate reads user-recipient rows at `edit` / `full` only, exactly as main does, so whatever is materialised to such a row counts in both forms and nothing else counts in either. The list read has no limit, and neither the engine nor a driver adds a default one, so several grant rows per record cannot truncate it.
- `public_read_write` and no-owner objects: decided once per call. With a queue column the rows are still read first, so a queue `allow` still wins over the `abstain`.
- Missing or deleted ids: no row, so no owner and no queue; the share and the bypass still decide, as per row.
- Duplicate ids: each index gets its own verdict. The row read's limit is the chunk length, which is at least the number of distinct ids.
- Mixed objects: not expressible, since a call names one object.
- Boundaries: 1,000 ids is one chunk. 1,001 is a chunk of 1,000 and a chunk of one, and the chunk of one takes the by-id read (`where { id }`, `limit: 1`). An empty list answers `[]` before any read.
- System context: `allow` for every id. A bypass-listed object: `abstain` for every id.
- Faults: a failure in the object-level tests denies every id the queue basis does not admit, which is what the per-row gate did. A thrown chunk read or share read denies that chunk. A thrown bypass lookup denies the ids still waiting.
- No path produces an `allow` the per-row gate would not: every `allow` comes from the same four tests on the same row, and the row and share lookups key on the exact id.

**`plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts`** (and the two host-wiring files) against the contract:
- Feature-detect is per verb, with `typeof … === 'function'`. Absent, the function answers `null` and the unchanged per-row loop runs (25 at a time, through `resolvePreImageFloorDrop`). A host double without `resolveKernelService` also falls back.
- The set path makes the same floor test once, builds the same context (`__writeScope`, the external grant patch), passes ids as strings as the per-row path does, and drops exactly the `allow` ids.
- An answer that is neither `allow` nor `deny` normalises to `abstain`. A throw or a wrong-length list is `deny` for all, logged once.
- Delegated callers are still not asked.

Nits. None changes a verdict on a path the tree reaches. N1 and N2 are worth a follow-up card; N3 and N4 can stay.

- N1 (nit) — the set form maps rows and shares back by exact id string, while the per-row gate takes whatever row the store's `=` returns. On a store that compares ids case-insensitively or pads spaces (MySQL's default collation), an id handed in a different spelling from the stored one finds its row per row and counts as missing in a set, so an owned row answers `deny` there. This is closed-direction only. The one in-tree caller passes ids it read from the store, so it does not reach this. Either note it in the docblock ("ids as the store returns them") or normalise.
- N2 (nit) — the owner-set and queue-membership promises are memoised for the call, a rejected one included. A transient failure in one chunk therefore denies every later chunk that needs the same lookup, where the per-row gate would ask again. Closed direction. The `writeVerdicts` docblock's "the other chunks keep their answers" is slightly too strong.
- N3 (nit) — the `checkEditMany` docblock's `allow` list names the queue basis and omits system context; the `checkEdit` docblock it points to names system context and omits the queue basis. The equality sentence governs, and the code agrees with both, but the two lists should match.
- N4 (nit) — the header of `security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts` still says exactly one function there is not a moved method body, and its list does not name `resolveSharingWriteVerdicts`.

For the lane seat (tests are its ACCEPT): the equivalence pin compares the set form with `checkEdit`, which is now the same function over one id, on an engine double. So it pins the list path against the one-id path. Equality with main's per-row gate rests on the existing `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` suite, and on the real-SQLite rig in plugin-security, which is small (4 and 60 rows). No case sits at exactly 1,001 ids; I read that path and it is correct.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, `Fixes #35934`. 9 files, +965/−116, ≤ 3000. Not governed, and no narrowing declared. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on `packages/spec/src/contracts`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, all three packages at patch. 3. **Gates**: contract record 7193294421 (`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, verified on the transcript) reads **PASS**, with no must-fix and no should-fix. The equivalence-matrix pin and 4 ablations each went red (os-dev report 7193076972). CI was still running when the record was read: 20 success, 11 skipped, 0 failed, 34 in progress.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd194d3ffcc734a0c0feb32dc86166ba97a12cd5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-sharing-verdicts.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts

Delta round on record 7193294421 (PASS at `14bf9f91`). The new head is one commit on `14bf9f91` and touches one file, `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.test.ts` (+11/−1). No file in Scope moved, so the earlier ①, ② and ④ stand as written. The earlier record had no must-fix and no should-fix, so there is no id to close.

Security-touching (sharing and authorization), as before. The delta changes a test double only; no verdict path moved.

Check-runs on this head when read: 12 success, 10 skipped, 14 in progress, 0 failed. The PR is a draft. The Test Core shards had not started (their plan job was still running), so the shard that timed out on `14bf9f91` has not been re-answered yet. Build Core, the four type checks and the lint families that carry `check:where-matcher` were also still running. This PASS is the design verdict; do not queue before those runs end green.

### ① Derived judgments

Unchanged. The delta publishes nothing: no source file, contract member, export or accept set moves.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). Unchanged. The changeset is untouched and `patch` on the three packages still matches what the diff publishes. A test-only commit owes no further changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Addendum 7194072292 carries no open question, `deviations: none` and `security_findings: none`. Its cause reading is consistent with the code: the double filtered each chunk's rows by rebuilding and scanning the `$in` list once per row, so a 1,000-id chunk cost about a million comparisons.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. No read in the service changed.
- The two out-of-scope answers in the earlier record (the `sharing-service.mdx` docs gap, and the stale cost paragraph in `.changeset/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`) are unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

The three points asked, by reading the delta and the double at the new head:

- **The Set cache does not weaken the pins.** `valueMatches` did `listOf(wanted).includes(key)` and now does `new Set(listOf(wanted)).has(key)`, cached. Both derive from the same `listOf` and the same `keyOf`, so membership is identical for every input:
  - an `$in` list, with or without repeats;
  - an object with no `$in`, or an array: an empty list before, an empty Set now, so no match either way;
  - a scalar or null: the `actual === wanted` branch, untouched.
  The double therefore matches exactly the rows it matched at `14bf9f91`. Its distance from the real engine's `$in` (ids compared as strings) is the same as before, not new.
- **Stale-cache risk: none reachable.** The WeakMap is keyed by the where leaf object (the `{ $in: […] }` wrapper), not by the array inside it. A stale answer would need the same leaf object handed to two finds with its array mutated in between. The double is reached only through `SharingService`, which builds a fresh where literal and a fresh spread copy of the ids for every find, so each read gets its own key. The cache lives per `makeVerdictEngine` call, so nothing carries across rigs.
- **Counted reads and the where-matcher gate are unchanged.** `noteRead`, `rowsNamed`, the read counters and every assertion in the counted-reads and fail-closed cases are byte-identical to `14bf9f91`. The combinator refusal in `storeFind` is untouched. No timeout was added.
- **Ablation 3 still goes red on reads.** Not run here (read-only). By reading: with `WRITE_VERDICT_CHUNK = 1` every chunk takes the one-id read, a scalar `where { id }` that the double answers by lookup, so the 10,000-record case finishes quickly and fails on `reads` being 10,000 where 10 is expected, and the queue case on 2,500 where 3 is expected. That agrees with the addendum's account (4 cases red, all on assertions).

One nit, new in this round:

- N5 (nit) — the cache comment and the addendum say "per list", but the key is the leaf object that holds the list. A future test that reuses one where object and mutates its array would read a stale Set. Nothing does so today. A word in the comment would cover it.

N1 to N4 of the earlier record are untouched by this commit and stand as nits.

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `bd194d3ffcc734a0c0feb32dc86166ba97a12cd5`
**ACCEPT** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5, delta round 1 (test-only)
